runs.question: Which OMB memo currently governs how federal agencies acquire AI, and what happened to the earlier acquisition memo?

answer.text:
The current governing memo is **OMB M-25-22, *Driving Efficient Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government***, dated April 3, 2025. It is issued under the Advancing American AI Act and Executive Order 14179 to help agencies acquire AI responsibly (EXECUTIVE OFFICE OF THE PRESIDENT OFFICE OF MANAGEMENT AND BUDGET WASHINGTON, D.C. 20503 THE DIRECTOR April 3, 2025 M-25-22; this memorandum provides guidance to agencies to improve their ability to acquire AI responsibly.).

The earlier acquisition memo, **M-24-18, *Advancing the Responsible Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government***, was formally superseded. M-25-22 withdraws it and takes its place, according to the document's own text (the April 2025 memo expressly withdraws and replaces OMB Memorandum M-24-18, Advancing the Responsible Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government.). Because M-25-22 replaces M-24-18, M-25-22 is the operative guidance.

Notes and limits:
- The retrieved passages do not state why M-24-18 was replaced. They also don't describe what M-25-22 changed in detail, so I can't say which M-24-18 requirements, if any, carried over.
- M-24-18 is labeled "October 2024" in its document title, but the memo text is dated September 24, 2024. The passages don't explain this discrepancy.
- Some M-24-18 material, such as its interoperability and vendor lock-in requirements, was current when issued. Whether M-25-22 keeps those requirements is not addressed in the retrieved passages.
